quotes.text: You can programmatically manage disputes using the API. With the API, you can upload evidence, respond to disputes, and receive dispute events using webhooks.
The combined character count for all text-based evidence field submissions is limited to 150,000.
Stripe distinguishes all disputes by a unique identifier, regardless of whether they’re related to a single payment.
When a payment has multiple disputes, use the `id` provided for each returned dispute in the list to make sure you’re responding to the correct dispute

When a dispute is created, Stripe sends a `charge.dispute.created` event. The [Dispute](https://docs.stripe.com/api/disputes/object.md) object exposes [charge](https://docs.stripe.com/api/disputes/object.md#dispute_object-charge) and a nullable [payment_intent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/disputes/object.md#dispute_object-payment_intent), but doesn’t include a direct reference to an invoice or subscription.

findings: The substantive November addition is a Handle dispute events section at new lines 91-93. It names charge.dispute.created and clarifies that the Dispute has a Charge reference and nullable PaymentIntent reference but no direct invoice or subscription reference. It routes subscription association to the subscription webhook guide rather than promising an in-object lookup. The current source's summary and related concept cover evidence and list/retrieve/update, not this important event/provenance boundary.

The new capture switches illustrative request examples from Node stripe.disputes.retrieve/update/list to curl for the same retrieve/update/list operations (old lines 16-22, 50-62, 83-103; new lines 17-20, 48-54, 75-87). Its example response is formatted as JSON-like text instead of old unquoted keys, but still contains an ellipsis and is illustrative, not a complete parseable API response. Do not infer Node SDK support was removed or the REST contract changed.

The same evidence rules persist: structured text versus file_upload ID fields, 150,000 combined text characters, dispute_evidence upload purpose, and catch-all uncategorized_text/uncategorized_file (old lines 64-73; new lines 56-65). These are field types and limits, not evidence acceptance or win guarantees.

Multiple disputes can still relate to one payment, with unique Dispute IDs; list by PaymentIntent or Charge and use the returned Dispute ID for the target retrieve/update (old lines 75-105; new lines 67-89). Neither payment filter is itself a subscription lookup.

The current source's Node snippets (lines 18-44) reflect May's examples. They may remain explicitly dated historical examples; a November update should identify curl as the newly captured example format and add the dispute event / nullable-reference boundary.
substantive_changes: New explicit charge.dispute.created event and Dispute object reference limits, with a route to subscription webhook guidance for invoice/subscription correlation (new lines 91-93).

Examples changed from Node SDK to curl for the same operations (old lines 16-22, 50-62, 83-103; new lines 17-20, 48-54, 75-87); this is presentation/sample-language change, not an established API capability change.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retrieve, update with evidence, and list by PaymentIntent or Charge remain the same operations despite example language changing (old lines 12-22, 46-62, 75-105; new lines 13-20, 44-54, 67-89).
Preserve the 150,000 combined text-character limit, file_upload ID and dispute_evidence upload purpose, and categorized evidence advice (old lines 64-73; new lines 56-65).
Preserve unique Dispute ID handling when more than one dispute concerns one payment; select the returned dispute ID before retrieve/update (old lines 75-105; new lines 67-89).
May's Node examples are historical sample code, not proof of a removed Node route; November shows curl samples for the same guide (old lines 16-22, 50-62, 83-103; new lines 17-20, 48-54, 75-87).
conflicts: The current source and disputes concept do not mention the new charge.dispute.created section or that payment_intent is nullable and there is no direct invoice/subscription field in the Dispute object (new line 93). A subscription-dispute query could otherwise mistakenly use the Dispute as a direct subscription locator.

New line 93's explicit no-direct-invoice/subscription statement should be retained with its scope; a Charge or PaymentIntent may be unrelated to a subscription, and the linked subscription webhook procedure has its own API-version and null-ID conditions.
unresolved_questions: The new guide links to, but does not itself specify, the full versioned procedure for resolving a dispute's associated subscription; this source should route to that guide rather than infer a universal direct field.
The captures do not establish that a given dispute concerns a subscription, that supplied evidence will be accepted, or that the dispute will be won.
The shift to curl examples does not establish a change to SDK availability or a required code migration.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/api, the November capture adds charge.dispute.created and explains that a Dispute has charge plus a nullable payment_intent but no direct invoice or subscription reference (new lines 91-93); [[source-stripe-disputes-api]] lacks that boundary. The May page ended after multiple-dispute selection and See also (old lines 75-111). The other conspicuous diff is Node examples becoming curl for the same retrieve, update and list operations, not a demonstrated API removal.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/api, [[source-stripe-disputes-api]] should preserve the May evidence limits and unique-dispute-ID selection (old lines 64-73, 75-105), repeated at new lines 56-65 and 67-89. Add the November event and nullable-reference warning at new line 93, with a route to the linked subscription webhook guide if a subscription must be identified. A listed Charge or PaymentIntent filter alone does not prove a subscription association or a dispute outcome.
